full_text_zh:
[P1] 传统童谣
连环画出版社
放风筝

[P2] 放风筝
金波/编选
胡永凯/图
连环画出版社

[P3] 放风筝
姐妹二人到城东，
到了城东去逛青，
捎带放风筝。
大姐放的花蝴蝶，
二姐放的活蜈蚣，
飘飘在天空，
好似一条龙。

[P4] 门后有个盆
门后有个盆，
盆里有个瓶。
乒隆乓啷一声响，
盆碰瓶，瓶碰盆，
也不知是盆碰坏了瓶，
也不知是瓶碰坏了盆。

[P5] 盖花楼
盖！盖！
盖花楼。
花楼低，
碰着鸡。
鸡下蛋，
碰着雁。
雁叼米，
碰着小孩就是你。

[P6] 十二月水果
正月甘蔗节节长，
二月青果两头黄，
三月梅子酸汪汪，
四月枇杷满街黄，
五月杨梅红如火，
六月莲蓬水中央，
七月红菱人人爱，
八月苹果装满筐，
九月栗子张开口，
十月金橘满园香，
十一月橘子红彤彤，
十二月里黄菱肉儿脆松松。

[P7] 蝴蝶姑娘嫁丈夫
呜嘟嘟，呜嘟嘟，
蝴蝶姑娘嫁丈夫。
谁奏乐？
知了吹箫蛙打鼓。
谁提灯？
小河边上萤火虫。
谁搀扶？
请了东庄螳螂姑。
谁护送？
蚂蚁哥哥带队伍。
小蜜蜂，嗡嗡嗡，
把她送进洞房中。

[P8] 一个蛤蟆一张嘴
一个蛤蟆一张嘴，
两只眼睛四条腿，
扑通一声跳下水。

两个蛤蟆两张嘴，
四只眼睛八条腿，
扑通，扑通，跳下水。

[P9] 云
云往南，
雨连连。
云往北，
一阵黑。
云往东，
一溜青。
云往西，
放牛小伙子披蓑衣。

[P10] 支起锣鼓唱秧歌

高高粗粗一棵麻，
两个蛐蛐往上爬。
一个蛐蛐爱喝酒，
一个蛐蛐爱喝茶。
酒也不喝，
茶也不喝，
支起锣鼓唱秧歌：
“唱得好来别说明，
唱得不好别打我。”

[P11] 小姑娘会梳头
小姑娘，会梳头，
一梳梳到麦子熟。
麦子磨成面，
芝麻磨成油，
黄瓜爬上架，
茄子打滴溜。

[P12] 月亮明
月亮明，月亮亮，
哥哥起来学木匠，
嫂嫂起来纳鞋底，
婆婆起来推糯米。
东一脚，西一脚，
一脚踩到母鸡婆。
母鸡展翅扑扑飞，
惊醒雄鸡叫喔喔。

[P13] 丫头丫
丫头丫，
打蚂蚱；
蚂蚱叫，
丫头笑；
蚂蚱飞，
丫头追；
蚂蚱蹦得高，
吓了丫头一大跳。

[P14] 风来咧
风来咧，
雨来咧，
蛤蟆背着鼓来咧。
什么鼓？
花花鼓，
乒乒乒乒二百五。

[P15] 一对蝈蝈吹牛皮
闲着没事上村西，
碰见两个蝈蝈吹牛皮。
大蝈蝈说：
“我在南山吃了只鸟。”
二蝈蝈说：
“我在北山吃了只鸡。”
大蝈蝈说：
“我在东山吃了只狗。”
二蝈蝈说：
“我在西山吃了头驴。”
大蝈蝈说：
“我在关外吃了个虎。”
二蝈蝈说：
“我在东海吃了鲸鱼。”
它两个吹得正起劲，
打南来了只大公鸡，
两个一见生了气，
伸伸腿，捋捋须，
一齐奔向公鸡去。
想吃公鸡没吃成，
“嘚儿”一声喂了鸡。
你猜为啥吃它俩？
谁叫它俩吹牛皮。

[P16] 小猫
小猫主意高，
跳到柳树梢。
细吹细打唱起来，
先唱鱼，后唱虾；
再唱公鸡、癞蛤蟆。
老虎听见要猫教，
小猫树上把头摇，
老虎气得双脚跳，
小猫树上哈哈笑。

[P17] 墙头草
墙头草，
风儿一来两边倒。
扶得东来西又倒，
扶得西来东又倒。
狗不吃，猫不咬，
枯了不能当柴烧。
full_text_en:
[P1] Traditional Children's Rhymes
Lianhuanhua Publishing House
Flying Kites

[P2] Flying Kites
Jin Bo / Editor and Compiler
Hu Yongkai / Illustrator
Lianhuanhua Publishing House

[P3] Flying Kites
Two sisters go to the east of the city,
To the east of the city to enjoy the spring,
And fly kites along the way.
The elder sister flies a colorful butterfly,
The younger sister flies a lively centipede,
Fluttering in the sky,
Like a dragon.

[P4] Behind the door, there's a basin.
Behind the door, there's a basin,
Inside the basin, there's a bottle.
With a loud 'ping pong pang',
The basin hits the bottle, the bottle hits the basin,
It's not known if the basin broke the bottle,
Or if the bottle broke the basin.

[P5] Build a Flower Pavilion
Build! Build!
Build a flower pavilion.
The pavilion is low,
It bumps into a chicken.
The chicken lays an egg,
It bumps into a goose.
The goose pecks at rice,
It bumps into a child — that's you.

[P6] Twelve Months of Fruits
In the first month, sugarcane grows tall and long,
In the second month, green fruits are yellow at both ends,
In the third month, plums are sour and juicy,
In the fourth month, loquats turn yellow all over the street,
In the fifth month, yangmei are red as fire,
In the sixth month, lotus pods float in the center of the water,
In the seventh month, red water chestnuts are loved by everyone,
In the eighth month, apples fill the baskets,
In the ninth month, chestnuts open their mouths,
In the tenth month, golden tangerines fill the garden with fragrance,
In the eleventh month, oranges are bright red,
In the twelfth month, yellow water chestnuts are crisp and tender.

[P7] Butterfly Girl Marries Her Husband
Doo-doo, doo-doo,
Butterfly girl marries her husband.
Who plays music?
Cicada plays flute, frog beats drum.
Who holds the lantern?
Fireflies by the little river.
Who helps her walk?
Invited the mantis girl from Dongzhuang.
Who escorts her?
Ant brother leads the team.
Little bee, buzz buzz buzz,
Take her into the bridal chamber.

[P8] One frog, one mouth
One frog, one mouth,
Two eyes, four legs,
Splish, splash, jumps into the water.

Two frogs, two mouths,
Four eyes, eight legs,
Splish, splash, jump into the water.

[P9] Clouds
Clouds go south,
Rain falls continuously.
Clouds go north,
A sudden darkness.
Clouds go east,
A streak of green.
Clouds go west,
The cowherd boy puts on his raincoat.

[P10] Set up gongs and drums to sing a folk song

Tall and thick, a hemp plant,
Two crickets climb up.
One cricket loves wine,
One cricket loves tea.
Neither drinks wine,
Nor drinks tea,
Set up gongs and drums to sing a folk song:
"If I sing well, don't say so,
If I sing poorly, don't hit me."

[P11] Little Girl Can Comb Her Hair
Little girl, can comb her hair,
Combing until the wheat ripens.
Wheat ground into flour,
Sesame ground into oil,
Cucumbers climb the trellis,
Eggplants drip and roll.

[P12] Moon Bright
Moon bright, moon shiny,
Brother gets up to learn carpentry,
Sister-in-law gets up to sew shoe soles,
Grandmother gets up to grind glutinous rice.
One step east, one step west,
One step steps on the hen.
The hen flaps its wings and flies,
Startling the rooster to crow 'cock-a-doodle-doo'.

[P13] Ya Tou Ya
Ya Tou Ya,
Chasing grasshoppers;
Grasshopper chirps,
Ya Tou laughs;
Grasshopper flies,
Ya Tou chases;
Grasshopper jumps high,
Startles Ya Tou with a big jump.

[P14] Wind is coming
Wind is coming,
Rain is coming,
A toad is coming with a drum on its back.
What kind of drum?
A flower drum,
Ping ping ping ping, two hundred and five.

[P15] A Pair of Grasshoppers Blowing Bubbles
Idling around, I went to the west of the village,
And met two grasshoppers blowing bubbles.
The big grasshopper said:
"I ate a bird in the southern mountain."
The little grasshopper said:
"I ate a chicken in the northern mountain."
The big grasshopper said:
"I ate a dog in the eastern mountain."
The little grasshopper said:
"I ate a donkey in the western mountain."
The big grasshopper said:
"I ate a tiger beyond the pass."
The little grasshopper said:
"I ate a whale in the East Sea."
They were blowing bubbles with great enthusiasm,
When a big rooster came from the south.
The two saw each other and got angry,
Stretched their legs, fluffed their beards,
And rushed toward the rooster together.
They failed to eat the rooster,
And with a "Dèr" sound, they fed the rooster.
Guess why they were eaten?
Because they were blowing bubbles.

[P16] Little Cat
Little cat has a high idea,
Jumps to the top of the willow tree.
Plays softly and sings,
First sings of fish, then shrimp;
Then sings of rooster, toad.
The tiger hears and wants to be taught,
Little cat shakes its head on the tree,
The tiger jumps in anger,
Little cat laughs on the tree.

[P17] Wall Grass
Wall grass,
When the wind comes, it falls to both sides.
Pushed east, it falls west;
Pushed west, it falls east.
Dogs won't eat it, cats won't bite it,
When dried, it can't be burned as firewood.
full_summary_zh:
[P1] 本页为绘本封面，左侧竖排黄色大字为“传统童谣”，右侧画面描绘了一个小女孩在红色背景下放风筝，风筝为一只大鸟，周围有蝴蝶和小鸟，底部横排白色大字为“放风筝”，右下角有“连环画出版社”字样。
[P2] 本页为绘本的扉页，显示书名《放风筝》，编选者为金波，绘图者为胡永凯，出版社为连环画出版社。页面左侧有一只色彩鲜艳的卡通老虎图案。
[P3] 本页描绘了两个小女孩在城东放风筝的场景，一个放蝴蝶风筝，一个放蜈蚣风筝，画面充满童趣和春天的气息。
[P4] 本页展示了一首传统童谣《门后有个盆》，画面描绘了一扇黄色木门和门后的一个红色盆，盆中放着一个青花瓷瓶，文字描述了盆与瓶相碰发出声响却不知谁碰坏了谁的有趣情景。
[P5] 本页展示了一首传统童谣《盖花楼》，画面描绘了一个色彩鲜艳的花楼和一个站在楼下的小孩，童谣通过连锁反应的想象，从盖楼到碰着小孩，充满童趣。
[P6] 本页展示了一首名为《十二月水果》的传统童谣，通过十二个月份对应不同水果的生长和特点，描绘了四季水果的丰富景象。画面左侧绘有多种水果，如甘蔗、苹果、莲蓬、栗子等，色彩鲜艳，充满童趣。
[P7] 本页展示了一首名为《蝴蝶姑娘嫁丈夫》的传统童谣，描绘了蝴蝶姑娘出嫁时，由知了、青蛙、萤火虫、螳螂姑和蚂蚁哥哥等小动物们分别奏乐、提灯、搀扶和护送的热闹场景，画面中绘有蝴蝶、蜜蜂、螳螂、青蛙和蚂蚁等卡通形象，背景为粉红色。
[P8] 本页展示了一首名为《一个蛤蟆一张嘴》的传统童谣，通过描述一只和两只蛤蟆跳入水中的情景，描绘了数量递增带来的声音变化，画面中绘有两只色彩鲜艳的蛤蟆跳入水中，溅起涟漪，背景为黑色，旁边有紫色花朵和绿叶。
[P9] 本页展示了一首名为《云》的传统童谣，通过描述云向不同方向移动时的天气变化，如南来雨、北来黑、东来青、西来需披蓑衣，画面描绘了一个色彩鲜艳的放牛娃和牛在山间，上方有不同形态的云朵，充满童趣和生活气息。
[P10] 本页展示了一首名为《支起锣鼓唱秧歌》的传统童谣，描绘了两只蛐蛐在麻秆上爬行，虽然一个爱喝酒、一个爱喝茶，但都不喝，而是支起锣鼓唱秧歌的有趣场景。画面中绘有两只色彩鲜艳的蛐蛐在绿色的麻秆上，背景为蓝色，充满童趣和生活气息。
[P11] 本页展示了一首名为《小姑娘会梳头》的童谣，描绘了小姑娘梳头时，麦子成熟、芝麻磨油、黄瓜爬架、茄子滴溜的田园景象，画面中绘有一个梳着辫子的小姑娘在瓜架下梳头，周围有黄瓜、茄子和麦穗，充满生活气息。
[P12] 本页展示了一首名为《月亮明》的传统童谣，描绘了月夜下家人各自忙碌的场景：哥哥学木匠、嫂嫂纳鞋底、婆婆推糯米，以及孩子玩耍时踩到母鸡，惊醒雄鸡啼叫的有趣画面。
[P13] 本页展示了一首名为《丫头丫》的童谣，描绘了一个小女孩追逐蚂蚱的有趣场景，画面中女孩在花草间奔跑，手持网兜，周围有蚂蚱和各色花朵，充满童趣和动感。
[P14] 本页展示了一首名为《风来咧》的童谣，描绘了风、雨来临，蛤蟆背着花花鼓到来的场景，画面中绘有一只色彩鲜艳、带有花纹的蛤蟆，背景为蓝色，四周有螺旋状图案，充满童趣和想象力。
[P15] 本页展示了一首名为《一对蝈蝈吹牛皮》的童谣，描绘了两只蝈蝈互相吹嘘吃了各种动物，最终被一只大公鸡吓跑的有趣场景。画面中绘有一只色彩斑斓的大公鸡和两只绿色的蝈蝈，背景为红色，充满童趣和想象力。
[P16] 本页展示了一首名为《小猫》的童谣，描绘了一只小猫跳到柳树梢上唱歌，老虎听见后想学，小猫却摇头拒绝，老虎气得跳脚，小猫在树上哈哈大笑的有趣场景。画面中绘有一只黑猫坐在柳树枝上，下方有一只黄色的老虎张着嘴，背景为红色，充满童趣和幽默感。
[P17] 本页展示了一首名为《墙头草》的童谣，描绘了墙头草随风摇摆、无依无靠的特性，画面中一只紫色的猫在瓦片屋顶上行走，上方有两只彩色的鸟，整体风格充满童趣和想象力。
